findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the exact `git config` invocation (including scope flag: `--local`, `--worktree`, or global) that must appear in the workflow, so the unit lint assertion and the implementation target the same command form.
evidence: AC1: 'sets merge.ours.driver=true for the tickets worktree' — scope (--local vs --worktree) unspecified
Why section: 'init.py:508-511 sets merge.ours.driver per clone' — implies --local but the workflow is a worktree add, not a clone
Git worktree shares .git of the parent; --local writes to the worktree's linked .git/config, --worktree writes to .git/worktrees/<name>/config — these have different precedence rules
findings.finding: The plan specifies that `reconcile-bridge.yml` must set `merge.ours.driver=true` 'for the tickets worktree' but does not state the git config scope or command form — `git config --local`, `git config --worktree`, or an environment approach. In a git worktree the effective config hierarchy differs from a standard clone, and the wrong scope silently fails to apply the driver.
scenarios: Agent uses `git config --local` inside the worktree directory but the driver isn't picked up because the worktree's gitdir is a file, not a directory, and the config target resolves unexpectedly.
Unit lint test only checks that the YAML contains the string 'merge.ours.driver=true', passing even if the scope flag is wrong — the defect survives to integration.
findings.suggested_fix: In AC1 or the Files section, add: 'The step must run `git -C <worktree-path> config --local merge.ours.driver true` (not --worktree, which requires git ≥2.34 and the .git dir to be a real directory).`

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the `tests/unit/workflow/` vs `tests/interfaces/store/` boundary is an enforced convention that requires the new workflow-lint assertions to be in a separate file, or whether they can be added as new test cases in the existing `test_reconcile_workflow_no_shallow_rebase.py` to avoid a second workflow-lint module.
evidence: Existing file `tests/interfaces/store/test_reconcile_workflow_no_shallow_rebase.py` already parametrises over `[reconcile-bridge.yml, reconcile-bridge-canary.yml]` for workflow-lint assertions of the same pattern (text-regex checks, no subprocess).
The new test file is described as 'unit workflow-lint assertion' — the same lint technique used in the existing file.
Rule-of-Three: only one existing workflow-lint file for this purpose; a second dedicated file brings it to two modules for five total assertions, below the threshold that would justify a new module.
findings.finding: The plan routes the two new unit workflow-lint assertions into a brand-new file (`tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py`) when the codebase already has `tests/interfaces/store/test_reconcile_workflow_no_shallow_rebase.py` — a parametrised workflow-lint file that already covers both reconciler workflows for exactly this category of text-inspection assertion. Creating a second workflow-lint module for two new cases is a premature-abstraction / Rule-of-Three violation unless the `tests/unit/` vs `tests/interfaces/store/` tier boundary is an enforced convention that prohibits colocating them.
scenarios: Author creates a new file, spreading the workflow-lint surface across two locations, making it non-obvious to future contributors that all workflow-lint tests live in one place.

If the tier boundary is NOT enforced, this split is gratuitous. If it IS enforced (e.g. `tests/interfaces/` requires a real git repo fixture and `tests/unit/` does not), the new file is justified — but the plan does not say which applies.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a positive rationale sentence explaining why a direct `git config` step (rather than calling `rebar init` as the canary does) is the right fix for `reconcile-bridge.yml` — e.g. that `rebar init` in the reconciler path would also write `.env-id` and commit `.gitattributes`/`.gitignore` if absent, adding unwanted side-effects to a workflow that deliberately does a bare worktree add.
evidence: Plan states the canary 'already gets merge.ours.driver via _merge_ours_unit' via rebar init, but never explains why the reconciler should NOT call rebar init instead of a raw git config line.

init_core() lines 239-271 show rebar init on an already-initialized tracker is fully idempotent: it runs _run_ensures_logged (which sets merge.ours.driver via _merge_ours_unit) without creating a branch or mutating ticket history.
ABSENCE: no 'we chose git config directly because...' statement anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The plan gives no positive rationale for why a surgical `git config merge.ours.driver=true` step is preferred over calling `rebar init` in reconcile-bridge.yml (the idiomatic path the canary uses). It only describes what currently exists, not why the chosen approach is the right design boundary — leaving implementers and future reviewers without a principled basis to resist re-aligning the reconciler with the canary's approach.
findings.location: ## Why / ## Files sections; no positive-rationale statement for chosen approach
scenarios: A future reviewer sees the reconciler uses a raw git config step while the canary uses rebar init, assumes inconsistency, and 'fixes' it by removing the git config step and adding rebar init — which would duplicate the canary's approach but could also introduce the ensure-registry's .env-id, gc-config, and gitattributes side-effects into the reconciler's boot path.
An implementer unsure of scope adds rebar init to reconcile-bridge.yml alongside the git config step, causing redundant work and a test assertion mismatch with AC #2.
findings.suggested_fix: In the ## Why section, add: 'The surgical `git config` approach is chosen over `rebar init` because `rebar init` on a fresh worktree would also commit `.gitattributes`/`.gitignore` and generate `.env-id` if absent — side-effects out of scope for a runner that intentionally does a bare worktree add and manages its own identity. The canary calls `rebar init` because it needs `.env-id` to drive `rebar create`/`rebar transition`; the reconciler does not.'
